provenance.deliberately_partial: Momentum-rate, collisions, non-ideal strings/pulleys and rotation are intentionally absent.

provenance.review_status: Author-created adaptation; independent academic review remains separate.

gates.title: Quantitative friction and connected-body constraints

canonical_concepts.statement: Static friction adjusts up to a limiting magnitude; equality with mu_sN is not automatic.
A common acceleration is a kinematic constraint justified by together-motion, not by Newton III.
Equal tension and endpoint-acceleration relations are conditional on an ideal string and its fixed-length geometry.

relations.expression: 0 <= f_s <= mu_s N; f_s,max = mu_s N; f_k = mu_k N
relations.meaning: Static friction adjusts up to a limit; the limiting equality and kinetic model apply only in their corresponding contact states.
conditions: The contact pair and relative sliding/tendency have been identified.
The normal reaction N belongs to that same contact in the current force state.
Use f_s = mu_s N only at the limiting/impending-slip state; otherwise static friction may be smaller.
Use f_k = mu_k N only when the adopted kinetic-friction model applies during relative sliding.

relations.expression: For bodies constrained to translate together along x: a_Ax = a_Bx = a_common
relations.meaning: A maintained together-motion constraint can link the relevant acceleration component while Newton II remains body-specific.
conditions: The bodies are constrained to remain in contact or otherwise translate together along the stated direction during the interval.
Each Newton-II equation is written for one chosen body in one consistent signed axis.
The common-acceleration equality applies only to the constrained component; other components are not silently equated.

relations.expression: Same ideal string: T_1 = T_2 = T; fixed-pulley length constraint x_1 + x_2 = constant gives a_1 + a_2 = 0
relations.meaning: One ideal massless inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley transmits one tension magnitude while fixed length links endpoint motion.

symbols.meaning: Tension magnitude along one continuous ideal string

conditions: The string is massless and inextensible.
The pulley is smooth and fixed.
The same continuous string is being referenced when one tension magnitude T is used.

For the bounded fixed-pulley geometry, total string length is constant so the two endpoint acceleration components along the string have equal magnitude and opposite sign in one common signed convention.

validity_conditions: Contact state is chosen before friction equality.
Body ownership is preserved before any system elimination.
Equal-tension/fixed-pulley relations require the declared ideal connection.

reasoning_sequence.action: Choose the contact/connection state and body boundaries.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Every quantitative equality in this slice is conditional on that physical setup.

reasoning_sequence.action: Write body-specific Newton-II equations and the appropriate friction or kinematic constraint.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Dynamics remains local to each chosen body while state/connection constraints link allowed unknowns.

reasoning_sequence.action: Check friction bounds, together-motion and fixed-string length after solving.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: A numerical solution that violates its assumed state is not physically valid.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: muN, equal acceleration or equal tension can be inserted automatically whenever the corresponding words appear.
misconceptions.counterexample: Static friction can be below its limit, bodies can slip relative to each other, and non-ideal pulleys can have unequal tensions.
misconceptions.repair: State the contact/connection condition that licenses each equality before using it.

problem_families.title: Friction-threshold, blocks-moving-together and ideal fixed-pulley questions
hidden_invariants: Static friction obeys a bound before its limit.
Together-motion supplies common acceleration, not Newton III.
Ideal fixed string supplies one T and a fixed-length acceleration constraint.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from the first symbol of the first relation.
